The test `['test.contrib.redshift_test.TestS3CopyToTable.test_s3_copy_with_nonetype_columns()']` checks whether the method `luigi.contrib.sqla.SQLActions.S3CopyToTable.copy` correctly handles cases where no columns are specified (`columns=None`). However, during the execution of this test, a `TypeError` occurred because `len(self.columns)` was called with `self.columns` being `None`. This is evident in the error message: "object of type 'NoneType' has no len()". Therefore, the bug lies in not handling the case where columns are not specified.

Following the execution path, we find that `luigi.contrib.redshift.RedshiftTarget` does not set a default value for `columns` when it is None. Consequently, when calling `self.copy(cursor, path)`, `self.columns` remains `None`, leading to the error demonstrated by the test.
